Command: An impure priest shall not eat holy food
Summary: The holy gifts (terumah) belonged to the priests, but a priest in impurity — from leprosy, a discharge, or touching uncleanness — was barred from eating them until cleansed (Leviticus 22:4-7).
Commandment: A priest unclean by leprosy, a discharge, or contact with uncleanness shall not eat of the holy things until he is clean.
Application: Holiness and impurity did not mix at the LORD's table: the priest's own cleansing came before his portion, and eating holy food in impurity profaned the holy name.
Purpose: Holy food was not to be eaten in impurity, keeping what is holy to the LORD distinct from uncleanness (Leviticus 22:2-4).
